Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

plancap 0.0.0.9000

Hamilton built out

  • Hamilton’s rulebook covers the whole plan: residential, centres, business and industrial zones, precincts, heritage, natural areas and the High Flood Hazard Area of Plan Change 14 (proposed, flagged), and runs city-wide.
  • New morphology settings density_area and far_area ("gross" or "net"): the land a density rule and a floor area ratio are measured on. The default, the whole site, keeps capacityengine’s results; Hamilton measures both on net site area, as its definitions say.
  • morphology$road_class_field: road boundaries are tagged with the class of the road in front, from the scenario’s centre lines, so a setback can name a road class.

A new jurisdiction, maps in 3D, documentation (stage 8)

  • Hamilton, New Zealand, entered through the Excel template from the Operative District Plan (revision of 13 November 2026, with Plan Change 12): General, Medium and High Density Residential, Business 6 and Business 2, every value cited, with seven rules registered as not modelled (rulebook_example("hamilton"), inst/extdata/hamilton_rulebook.xlsx). The vignette “Adding a new jurisdiction: Hamilton” follows it from the plan text to results, including a “permitted activities only” scenario.
  • view_capacity_3d(): an interactive 3D map (mapgl), sites raised to their height or each storey’s footprint at its level, coloured by capacity per hectare.
  • plot_capacity_map() and plot_change_map() take basemap = TRUE (Esri’s World Gray Canvas, or any maptiles provider).
  • Fixed: a blank Excel template’s families sheet had no family column.
  • Vignettes: “Writing a rulebook”, “Rule reference”, “Preparing sites”, “Method and assumptions”; the README describes the package as built.

Plots (stage 7)

  • One theme, theme_capacity() (light or dark), and one palette system, capacity_palette() and the scale_*_capacity_*() scales: eight categorical hues in a fixed order validated for colour vision deficiency (a ninth category folds into “Other”), a one-hue sequential scale and a blue and red diverging scale with a grey midpoint. Zones keep their colour from plot to plot. Text is never in a series colour; captions state what the figures are.
  • Capacity plots: plot_capacity() (ranked bars, stacked or faceted), plot_height_profile(), plot_distribution(), plot_constraints() (the waterfall), plot_capacity_map() (sites, grid or areas, per hectare), plot_cumulative() (the capacity curve), plot_site() (plan or axonometric) and autoplot() (a four-plot dashboard, with patchwork).
  • Comparison plots: plot_comparison() (dumbbell or change bars), plot_change_map(), plot_transitions() and plot_attribution(); plot_sensitivity().
  • Fixed: envelope geometry (keep_geometry = TRUE) labelled storeys wrongly when more than one site was built.
  • The vignettes show the plots; “Summaries” is now “Summaries and plots”.

Comparing scenarios (stage 6)

  • scenario_set() and run_scenarios(): scenarios run together, the baseline in full and the others incrementally from it. read_scenarios() reads a whole comparison from a YAML manifest.
  • compare_scenarios(): totals and change; every baseline site’s change with a reason (rezoned, rule_changed, overlay_added, overlay_removed, area_changed, neighbour_effect, parcel_changed, unchanged), with changed parcels apportioned to the baseline’s by area; zone transitions; by zone, height band, area and grid; land reconciliation; and attribution of the change to its drivers (rules, zoning, layers, parcels), sequential or Shapley, with the rules driver split by each zone, overlay or area whose rules changed. Sites are compared by landholding (scenario(landholding = )).
  • diff_inputs(): the rule changes as a table, and the land rezoned, the layer land added or removed and the parcels changed as polygons. check_comparison() reconciles every view.
  • Exampleton Plan Change 1 (exampleton_pc1(), rulebook_example( "exampleton_pc1"), and a manifest in extdata): a rulebook that extends: the operative one, a rezoning, a wider flood plain and a re-subdivided block. Vignette “Comparing plan changes”.
  • Boundaries are cut where they cross a distance from the road that a rule switches at (within_frontage, beyond_frontage), so each part takes its own rule (capacityengine item 321), for the standards being built. This changes Exampleton’s figures: MDR’s front exemption standard now applies its plane behind 20 m on every side boundary.
  • Incremental runs: an exclusion layer’s change reaches only the sites it touches; a run copying every site keeps its storey stack’s columns.
  • Fixed: summarise_capacity(by = "area") replaced the land area with the area names.
  • The capacityengine converter carries applies_to_rear_sites: true (rear sites only).
  • Gate: operative against PC120 (residential standards) on the Auckland tile reproduces capacityengine’s change exactly, on every landholding.

Summaries (stage 5)

  • summarise_capacity(): capacity by any site column or by zone, storeys, height, site size or floor area ratio bands, binding constraint, polygons (areas), a square grid, or floor area by storey level; measures include floor area by use, dwellings, means and medians, floor area ratio, per hectare figures and shares. Spatial summaries return sf.
  • summary() of a capacity result: headline, by zone, flags and what limits dwellings. capacity_table() formats any summary with gt.
  • constraint_breakdown(): a waterfall from the theoretical maximum (whole site, every storey the height allows) to the enabled floor area: storeys not reached, setbacks and land, each cap, floor area ratio and maximum site floorspace. The steps add up exactly.
  • explain_site(): one site’s rules, boundaries, setbacks at every storey with their citations, storeys and dwellings.
  • sensitivity(): a rule swept through values (or whole rules), with incremental reruns.
  • check_capacity(): reconciliation (parcels, land, storeys against sites, uses against floor area) and diagnostics; unmodelled_report(): the register of rules not modelled.
  • Envelopes record storeys_allowed; capacity results keep their scenario and options.
  • Vignettes: “Getting started” and “Summaries”.

Shape, access and the measured front yard (stage 4, part 5)

  • site_shape_factor(): a zone’s site_shape rectangle must fit clear of the yards, water yards and exclusions for a site to create vacant sites; estimate_capacity() caps the subdivision paths by it (defaults$site_shape_factor).
  • find_access_widths(): the access width of rear sites, from their own entrance strip, easements (scenario(easements = )) and access lots (scenario(other_parcels = )); the access width table reads it, and pieces of one landholding (scenario(landholding = )) share their best access.
  • yard(value_from = "existing_front_setback"): a front yard set by the average setback of the dwellings on the neighbouring sites along the street, measured from building outlines (find_existing_front_setbacks(), scenario(buildings, streets, neighbours)); where nothing is measured the rule is reported as not applied. The Auckland rulebook’s Special Character front yard now carries it.
  • Morphology rear_site_sides_as_rear: a rear site’s side boundaries are rear boundaries where the plan defines a rear site’s yards as rear yards (AUP J1); on in the converted rulebooks.
  • Height surfaces are banded for all sites in one pass (13 times faster on the gate tile); ground tables may match segments by midpoint (x, y).
  • Fixed: an open-ended band of an access width table (or any band table) read its upper limit from a field beginning “max” by partial matching.
  • plancap now reproduces capacityengine exactly on the gate tile (floor area and dwellings on all 2,680 sites, with terrain, height surfaces and the measured front yard).

Terrain and towers (stage 4, part 4)

  • Stepped terrain (the default, defaults$terrain): each site’s ground is a plane fitted to its boundaries’ ground; a recession plane is measured from the ground at its own boundary, taken over runs of near-straight pieces of one boundary, and the ground’s rise into the site slows the building’s gain on the plane. terrain = "flat" stands the building on one floor at the site’s mean ground.
  • Ground levels may be supplied as tables (scenario(ground = )) instead of a DEM; a DEM is now sampled along each boundary, not at its midpoint.
  • A tower floorplate limit caps storeys above the tower threshold; tower plan dimension and separation are counted in the run report as not modelled.
  • Reproduces capacityengine with terrain and height surfaces on the gate tile to +0.034% of floor area (99.2% of sites exact).

Reproducing capacityengine (stage 4, part 3)

  • On a 2,680-site Auckland tile, on flat ground, plancap reproduces capacityengine’s floor area to +0.033% (99.4% of sites to 0.01 m2) and its dwellings to -0.5% (data-raw/gate/).
  • zone_family(): a family that counts across a boundary only where the contiguous area of its zones there is within bounds (rules next to small or large open space).
  • A zone stating no storey count divides its height into as many default-height storeys as fit (20 m: six storeys of 3.33 m).
  • A site with no road frontage is left uncapped by the access width table and flagged (access_unmeasured).

Heights, surfaces and building form (stage 4, part 2)

  • Height overlays follow capacityengine’s rules: an override replaces total and occupiable height; a cap lowers total height and lowers occupiable height only where its value is lower (a cap that bites only the roof allowance leaves the storeys); a cap over a zone with no height caps nothing. Overlays may carry a height_conversion table from mapped total height to occupiable height (Auckland’s Height Variation Control).
  • Height surfaces (rasters, as elevations with a dem or as heights above ground): a surface covering a whole site caps its height at the lowest point; one covering part takes, at each storey, the land the surface is too low for.
  • Building length and separation cut gaps through the footprint, from the height separation starts (building_separation may be bands by height).
  • Height bonuses are built as a second, incremental envelope and reported in the *_with_bonus columns.

Capacity (stage 4, part 1)

  • estimate_capacity() turns envelopes into floor area (split between residential and business by each zone’s use and residential share, by storey where it changes) and dwellings, by volumetric, density, hybrid and large-site paths; then floor area ratio and maximum site floorspace (capping the stack from the ground up), no dwellings without a buildable envelope or on land overlays remove, dwellings per site, the access width cap, minor dwellings, area totals (including sub-areas sharing a total), and entitlements as a floor. Bonuses are reported in *_with_bonus columns.
  • Exclusion overlays: removes: all takes land off the buildable ground; removes: residential keeps floor area over it out of dwellings.

The envelope engine (stage 3)

  • build_envelopes() builds each site’s storey stack: storeys at the zone’s own storey height, each tested at its ceiling; one setback per boundary per storey (the deepest any applicable rule asks); a single clip with reflex corners filled; coverage and landscaping as shares of net site area; floorplate caps; a stack that never widens and ends below the minimum floorplate. Water yards are measured from the water; access legs come off the buildable ground.
  • Rules are resolved per site: zone, then precincts and sub-areas (which replace), then parameter overlays and height overlays. A change replaces whole fields such as height, and replaces only the setback kinds it names.
  • Alternative standards are built separately and each site takes the most enabling (or the one named by variant_choice).
  • keep_setbacks = TRUE returns, for every boundary at every storey, the setback applied and the rule and citation that set it.
  • Incremental runs: given a baseline, sites whose inputs are unchanged are copied; the result equals a full run.
  • Reproduces capacityengine’s hand-worked envelope figures through the converted Auckland rulebook.

Scenarios and site preparation (stage 2)

  • scenario() bundles a rulebook with its parcels, roads, zoning and other layers; scenario_change() describes a plan change as what differs from a base scenario.
  • prepare_sites() turns a scenario into sites in two cached steps: parcel geometry (depends only on parcels, roads, water, centrelines and ground) and plan geometry (zoning, overlays, areas). A rule-only change reuses both; a zoning change reuses the first.
  • Morphology helpers, each returning its evidence: find_road_frontages(), find_side_rear(), find_corner_sites(), find_through_sites(), find_rear_sites(), find_access_legs(), find_water_boundaries(), find_road_widths() and site_metrics(). Boundaries have a class (road, side, rear) and tags (reserve, riparian, coastal, lakeside, zone boundary).
  • Sites crossed by a zone boundary are split (slivers merged, unzoned remainders kept); the zone across each boundary is found by probing outward, across the carriageway for road frontages.
  • check_morphology() compares classification shares with usual ranges; plot_morphology() draws them.

Rulebooks (stage 1)

  • A rulebook holds every planning rule for one plan, with a citation for every value: rulebook(), zone(), height_limit(), ratio(), bands(), building_form(), density(), use_mix(), overlay(), area(), sub_area(), bonus(), entitlement(), unmodelled_rule(), and the add_*() and set_*() functions.
  • Setback rules all reduce to a required distance as a function of height: yard(), plane() (including planes graded by orientation, planes that turn vertical, and planes measured from the far side of a road), upper_level_setback(), proportional_setback() and setback_profile(), evaluated with setback_distance(). Rules apply under conditions().
  • Any value may be a restricted formula such as "max(3, 0.4 * H)" (eval_rule_value()).
  • Rulebooks read and write losslessly as YAML, JSON and Excel (read_rulebook(), write_rulebook(), rulebook_template()), with extends: for scenarios and plan changes. A JSON Schema checks structure; validate_rulebook() also checks references and missing citations.
  • rule_table() lists every rule with its source; set_rule() and extend_rulebook() change rules for what-ifs; convert_rulebook_units() converts between metres and feet, formulas included.
  • Shipped rulebooks: Exampleton, plus Auckland (operative Unitary Plan, all 217 precincts), Christchurch and Wellington as dated worked examples converted from the capacityengine project (rulebook_example()).

Example data (stage 0)

  • Package skeleton, continuous integration and documentation site.
  • The Exampleton synthetic town: exampleton(), exampleton_layer(), exampleton_layers(), exampleton_dem() and exampleton_path().
